work_order.approach: Fix the two QA-proven root causes with different approaches from attempt 1, and carry forward that attempt's two passing fixes unchanged. BUG-1: Field generates its input id from the field name alone (field-${name}), so the members page renders two inputs with id field-name and fills/submits hit the wrong one. Field now derives a unique id per instance with React useId so each label targets exactly its own input; RenameGroupForm keeps its state.ok refresh effect, which becomes observable once the submit is fixed. BUG-2: RemoveButton called router.refresh() in the awaited continuation of the wrapped Server Action, before useActionState commits the ok state that renders the status. RemoveButton now follows the ArchiveButton precedent exactly: the wrapped action only returns the result, and a useEffect on state.ok commits the 'Removed <name>.' status render first and then calls router.refresh() once (announced-ref guarded). The money sign-carry and readMembers EXISTS-predicate fixes from attempt 1 passed QA (T-1, T-2) and are carried forward unchanged.

work_order.root_cause: Two wrong diagnoses in attempt 1, both proven by QA evidence. (1) Rename: the plan blamed a missing router.refresh, but QA captured the Server Action request carrying the field's INITIAL value on the base commit — refresh can never fix a submit that sends the wrong value. The true cause is a duplicate DOM id: Field builds id as field-${name}, and the members page renders two Field name='name' inputs, so fills land in the placeholder field and Save submits the rename form's untouched value with a false 'Saved.'. (2) Removal: the plan assumed the status insertion commits before the async refresh lands, but the PR calls router.refresh() in the action's awaited continuation BEFORE useActionState commits the ok state — on a fast connection the refresh wins and the row unmounts with zero insertions, exactly QA's intermittent signature.

work_order.understanding: Attempt 1 (previous-work-order.json v1, PR #21) was wrong on both browser defects, and QA's evidence proves it. First, the plan diagnosed rename staleness as a missing router.refresh(); but QA captured the Server Action body carrying the INITIAL name on base commit 7390e3e, and the T-7/T-4 trees show the typed value in the placeholder 'Name' input while the rename input kept the old value with a false 'Saved.'. The true cause is Field's id = field-${name} colliding across the two same-named fields on the members page. Second, the plan assumed the 'Removed' insertion commits before the refresh; but the PR dispatches router.refresh() in the wrapped action's continuation before useActionState commits ok state, so the refresh intermittently wins (T-9/T-10/T-11). The money and readMembers fixes passed QA and are carried forward; only the Field-id and removal-ordering approaches change.

qa.actual: The multipart Server Action request carries the field's INITIAL group name no matter what is visible in the input. Verified at the request level: clearing the field, typing 81 characters, and typing a valid new name all submit the original name; the server renames to the submitted (unchanged) name and returns ok:true, so the form shows a false 'Saved.' while the stored name never changes. Reproduced identically on the base commit 7390e3e served from a clean worktree, so the defect predates this PR.
qa.expected: Clicking Save submits the value visible in the field: an empty name is refused with 'Enter a name for this group.', an 81-character name with 'That name is too long.', and a valid new name is stored, after which the surrounding names update.
repro: Sign up as a fresh synthetic user on the preview and create a group.
Open the group's members page and change the Group name field to a new value (typed character by character, exactly as a user would).
Click Save and capture the POST request body.
Observe the multipart body carries the ORIGINAL name in the name field, 'Saved.' appears, and after a reload the back-link still shows the original name.
